- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.11) and recent history shows upward momentum.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially < -0.22) or after a recent spike, especially if followed by a sharp drop.
- Overshoot after spikes: if model peaks sharply after a recent high, reduce forecast by 5–10% in the next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is consistently above 80–85% of recent 10-day average, adjust downward by 2–5%.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment was negative 2–3 days prior, reduce forecast by 3–7% to account for delayed market reaction.
- Horizon-specific: for 30-day forecasts, avoid overconfidence in early days (1–5) after a spike; cap forecast at 10% below recent 10-day high.
